name: Hotel Highlands Park
why_it_matters: TripAdvisor's #1-ranked Gulmarg restaurant — a stone-cottage dining room with wood-burning fireplaces and meadow views. Rogan josh and saag nadru (lotus stem) are the dishes locals come for; the Cantonese line is unexpectedly competent.
insider_tip: The restaurant is open 7:30am-11pm but the dining room fills with hotel guests at 8pm — book a 7:30pm table or come at 9:30pm to avoid the rush. Cottage cluster gets cold; ask for a table near the wood-burner.
signature_address: Church Road, Gulmarg 193403, Baramulla District, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Bakshi Restaurant
why_it_matters: TripAdvisor's #2 in Gulmarg — the bazaar-side spot where locals actually eat. View of the Maharani Temple, Kashmiri Wazwan staples done plainly and well. Mirchi mutton and rishta are the dishes the kitchen takes pride in.
insider_tip: It gets busy and the pace is slow — order the pulao the moment you sit down (it takes 25 minutes). Vegetarians: the kashmiri rajma and dum aloo are both made fresh and worth the wait.
signature_address: Main Market, Forest Block, Near Police Station, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Cloves
why_it_matters: All-day fine-dining at The Khyber Himalayan Resort — Kashmir's only resort whose Wazwan is plated on a traditional copper tarami at the table. The kitchen does a vegetarian Wazwan tarami too, which most Wazwan kitchens won't.
insider_tip: Reserve through the resort even if you're not staying — non-resident dining is allowed but capacity is limited. The dinner Wazwan needs to be ordered 24 hours ahead; the à la carte rogan josh is on every day.
signature_address: Lobby Level, The Khyber Himalayan Resort & Spa, H-3 Gulmarg, 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Chaikash Tea Lounge
why_it_matters: The Khyber's tea lounge — named after the Kashmiri word for soaked tea leaves. Floor-to-ceiling windows onto the snow-line, fireplace seating, traditional samovar service for kahwah. The closest thing Gulmarg has to a high-altitude Salon de Thé.
insider_tip: Skip the dinner crowd — come for afternoon high tea (3-5pm) when the kahwah comes with a tier of saffron biscuits and bakerkhani. Non-resort guests welcome but it's quieter mid-week.
signature_address: The Khyber Himalayan Resort & Spa, H-3 Gulmarg, 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Nedous Dining Room
why_it_matters: The dining room of Nedou's Hotel — Asia's first organised hotel group, founded 1888 by Michael Nedou. Wooden floors, wooden pillars, hunting laurels on the walls; the food is straight Kashmiri-Mughlai cooked the way it was for the Maharaja's guests.
insider_tip: Pair dinner with a single malt at Hunter's Bar next door (Yamazaki, Hibiki listed) — the same hotel, same heritage, but the bar charges separately. Ask for a window table; Gulmarg's snowline starts where the lawn ends.
signature_address: Nedou's Hotel, Forest Block, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: The Hunter's Bar
why_it_matters: The bar at Nedou's — one of the few colonial-era bar rooms in Kashmir still operating. Hunting prints, fireplace, floor-to-ceiling glass onto the Apharwat range. The Yamazaki and Hibiki on the back-bar are unusual for a hill-station hotel.
insider_tip: Order a hot toddy at the fireplace seats after a snow day — they make it with local honey and Kashmiri saffron. Bar opens 5pm; arrive early in winter when daylight goes by 5:30pm to catch the sunset over the meadow.
signature_address: Nedou's Hotel, Forest Block, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: 1860 Restaurant
why_it_matters: Named for the year the Maharaja first lent his royal Jhelum boats to European travellers — the unofficial start of Kashmir tourism. The restaurant at The Vintage Gulmarg trades on that history with traditional Indian cooking and a build-your-own-menu format.
insider_tip: The 'create your own menu' option is real — useful for families with mixed eaters. Continental and Chinese hold up but the Kashmiri-Mughlai is the kitchen's strength; stick to it.
signature_address: First Floor, The Vintage Gulmarg, 2739 Circular Road, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Northwind Cafe
why_it_matters: The pizza outlier in a town of Wazwan and Maggi. 5.0/5 on TripAdvisor's pizza ranking — wood-fired thin-crust made fresh, with veg options that aren't just paneer. The cafe Gulmarg locals send foreign skiers to.
insider_tip: Veg-friendly travellers note: Gulmarg's restaurants tend to default to mutton and Maggi. Northwind is the rare place where a vegetarian pizza is the kitchen's actual specialty, not an afterthought.
signature_address: Hard Aboora, Gulmarg Town, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Dasterkhwan
why_it_matters: The Kashmiri-Mughlai room at Hotel Hilltop — one of three on-site dining rooms (Chopstick for Chinese, Big Bite for fast food, Miasa for cafe). Dasterkhwan keeps the focus tight: Wazwan staples for hotel guests and walk-ins.
insider_tip: Hotel Hilltop runs four kitchens under one roof — useful for families splitting between Wazwan, Chinese, pizza and shisha. Order Dasterkhwan's rogan josh and a Chopstick chilli chicken if your group is mixed.
signature_address: Hotel Hilltop, Gondola Road, Forest Block, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir

name: Dilkusha at Heevan Retreat
why_it_matters: First-floor multi-cuisine restaurant at Heevan Retreat, a short walk from the gondola base. Useful for ski-day lunches that aren't the gondola-base Maggi stalls. Carries a separate Gujarati thali — rare in Kashmir, useful for jain/no-onion-garlic travellers.
insider_tip: Skiers heading up the gondola: Heevan's Dilkusha does proper hot lunches with rogan josh and kashmiri pulao at sane prices, 5 minutes' walk from the gondola queue. Better than the chai-and-Maggi options at the base on a cold day.
signature_address: Heevan Retreat, Gondola Road, Gulmarg 193403, Jammu and Kashmir
